speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my office. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to better understand the underlying cause, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have worsened over time?

REQUEST TEST: Full neurological examination focusing on coordination, reflexes, and sensory function.
REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count and metabolic panel.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information, but I must rely on my own evaluation rather than previous suggestions; have you noticed any numbness, vision changes, or issues with bladder control accompanying your ataxia?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain and Cervical Spine with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are pathognomonic for PML, caused by JC virus reactivation, which explains the progressive gait and limb ataxia. Do you have any history of immunosuppression, such as HIV, chemotherapy, or long-term steroid use?
